explanation: Build cumulative probability endpoints, draw uniformly in [0,1), and find the first endpoint strictly greater than the draw. The interval lengths encode the requested distribution; strict comparison skips zero-width intervals.
timeComplexity: O(n) per call: building n endpoints dominates O(log n) binary search. The bound includes all probability processing performed anew on each draw, rather than assuming precomputed endpoints.
spaceComplexity: O(n) temporary prefix endpoints. The linear scan keeps only a draw and running threshold; binary-search variants retain n prefix endpoints.
attribution: Unmodified reference from epi_judge_python_solutions/nonuniform_random_number.py; Elements of Programming Interviews Judge contributors; CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 International, retained in repository LICENSE. Explanation authored for EPI Practice.
correctness: For prefix endpoints p, value i owns [p[i−1],p[i]). Upper-bound search returns exactly that interval, including at a repeated endpoint. Its length is probabilities[i], so an ideal uniform draw selects i with that probability.
walkthrough: For values [4,9] with probabilities [0.25,0.75], draws below 0.25 return 4 and draws from 0.25 onward return 9. A draw of 0.6 therefore returns 9; repeated draws select 9 three times as often on average. JSON arguments are [values,probabilities]. Observed true validates repeated samples; the callable returns one value. Finite samples do not prove exact randomness.
edgeCases: One value is always selected when its probability is one.
The validator checks repeated samples rather than one fixed output.
